description:
The business the user NAMED, by name matching only: case, punctuation, possessives and articles are
ignored, the words may come in any order, a part of the name is enough («Bern’s» finds «Bern’s Steak
House»), up to two typos per word, and Cyrillic is transliterated. No meaning, no ranking: `found` is
ordered by exactness, then — with a `location` — inside the radius first and nearer first. Several
places with one name all come back with their addresses; without a location and across cities the
answer asks which place. `found: []` means the business is NOT in this catalogue; then
`nearby_in_same_niche` lists up to five cards of the trade the name suggests, every one marked
`not_the_requested_business: true` — never present them as the business asked for.
The best matches carry `task_card` (≤ 2.5 KB): `time` for `needed_by` (else `hours_today`), up to 5 `items`
under `query`, `terms`, `deliver_to`, and `next` {promise[], candidate[], action}. `intent` (book / order /
quote / info) chooses the action. The full menu is get_card.

deliver_to.description: where it must be brought (a postcode is best): the card says confirmed / refuted / unknown

intent.description: what the user means to do with this business

location.description: a postcode, a city or "lat,lng" — orders the matches by nearness and bounds the nearby list

name.description: the business name as the user said it

needed_by.description: when: «sunday», «tomorrow 19:00», «now», «tomorrow after 15:00» — read on the business’s own clock, three ways (on_day / open_at / slot_after)

query.description: the thing under the task («red roses», «ribeye»): picks the ≤ 5 items on the card

name: find_business
title: A business by its name
